source_review.notes: Checked the primary GFS, Ceph, and Windows Azure Storage papers or official summaries plus current official HDFS, Ceph, CRUSH, placement-group, and Colossus documentation. Sources support logical chunks/blocks, namespace/data-path separation, direct storage-node access, placement epochs, inventory, integrity, failure domains, rebalance, and repair claims. All ten URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed ordered file extents, handle/generation, fixed-size block count and interval coverage, range intersection, placement epoch/function, observed inventory, replication amplification, and availability/protection predicates.
Checked half-open intervals, zero-length file/range boundaries, ceiling division, tail length, and intra-block offsets.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical block identity, physical location, byte extent, replica state, and namespace version remain distinct.

evidence: Executed block-extent-accounting with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced 288,358,400 file bytes, three block lengths, 865,075,200 replicated bytes, factor 3.00, both range fragments, and 134,217,728 repair bytes.
Recomputed exercise one as four blocks of 128, 128, 128, and 26 MiB and the 250–280 MiB range as six MiB from block one plus 24 MiB from block two.
Recomputed 30 PiB payload divided by 0.85 as approximately 35.294 PiB and distinguished that convention from adding 15 percent to obtain 34.5 PiB.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Fixture and exercises use binary MiB/PiB explicitly and omit physical overhead unless named.

evidence: Derived dense block count by ceiling division and proved exact ordered nonoverlapping coverage including a partial tail.
Derived range fragments from intersections between a requested half-open interval and each block extent.
Derived payload replication amplification as r while preserving the caveat that real physical capacity includes additional positive and negative terms.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Arithmetic indices describe extent geometry and never substitute for metadata-resolved durable handles.

evidence: Reviewed empty, exact-multiple, partial-tail, one-byte, cross-boundary, invalid, sparse, compressed, copy-on-write, immutable, mutable, append-only, and virtual-block cases.

Reviewed rename, snapshot, pathname reuse, stale generation/map/report, incomplete write, ambiguous acknowledgement, lost/corrupt/orphan/misplaced/excess replicas, concurrent rebalance, and delayed repair instructions.

Reviewed same-host/rack correlation, latent cold corruption, giant-object skew, hot reads, full targets, background repair contention, unauthorized handles, tenant leakage, key retirement, and research-data retention/deletion.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Namespace, placement, inventory, integrity, authorization, lifecycle, and physical allocation boundaries are separately addressed.

evidence: Traced generation-qualified handles, extent coverage, map epoch, authorized placement, exact length/checksum, commit visibility, inventory reconciliation, failure-domain protection, repair ordering, and tombstone grace through exposition and exercises.
Checked that only current compatible verified replicas count toward protection and that repair completes before obsolete-copy removal.
Checked that acknowledgement level, availability, durability, semantic validity, and retention approval are not conflated.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter does not infer authority from path, ordinal, location, block report, file presence, or desired policy.

evidence: Reviewed all ten block-layer audit obligations from abstraction naming through consequence review.

Checked counterexamples for block-equals-sector, path-equals-content, location-equals-identity, computed-equals-timeless, report-equals-authority, checksum-equals-redundancy, allocated-equals-committed, timeout-equals-failure, orphan-equals-deletable, and aggregate-free-space-equals-writable claims.
Reviewed extent reconstruction, commit, integrity, inventory reconciliation, protection, scrub, repair, and capacity arguments.
proof_review.notes: Logical correctness, byte integrity, durability, availability, performance, security, and domain governance remain distinct evidence obligations.

evidence: Audited uses of exact, complete, valid, current, authoritative, durable, available, protected, safe, and prove.
Confirmed fixture calculations are labeled as a dense fixed-boundary model rather than a production protocol, physical allocation forecast, or erasure-coding analysis.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Current product behavior is scoped to dated official documentation.

evidence: Reviewed retrieval dates, workload/block/range distributions, topology snapshots, inventory/report epochs, scrub evidence, capacity terms, foreground/background metrics, repair trials, and tail requirements.
Confirmed no production durability, universal block-size optimum, performance, research-ethics approval, certification, or external-review claim is made.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production claims require exact implementation, media/topology, protection policy, workloads, faults, retained versions, security controls, and repeated recovery evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed storage layers, logical extents, handles/generations, namespace, placement, inventory, commit, integrity, reconciliation, balance, repair, scrub, capacity, security, and evidence as one coherent block-storage model.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed block sizing, direct data paths, explicit/computed placement, epoch handling, acknowledgement levels, node reports, discrepancy states, repair ordering, scrub policy, capacity headroom, background interference, tokens, quotas, and telemetry. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from storage-layer vocabulary through extent math, architecture, lifecycle, integrity, operations, and capacity; ten examples and five complete answers cover calculation, identity design, diagnosis, sizing, and unfamiliar research-archive transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external distributed-storage researcher, filesystem practitioner, storage vendor, security auditor, research-ethics authority, archival specialist, or certification review is claimed.
